key_insight: All four deep generative models reconstruct the mean of a non-stationary Gaussian random field, but they differ substantially in how well they recover its covariance structure.
engineering_relevance: For spatio-temporal modeling workflows, this paper shows that matching visual sample quality is not enough; covariance diagnostics are essential to validate uncertainty and non-stationarity in generated fields.
method: Benchmarked flow matching (FM), DDPM, score-SDE, and VAE on a known non-stationary Gaussian random field.
Compared generated samples against oracle samples and a stationary control using mean and covariance recovery metrics.
Extended the validation framework to ERA5 temperature anomalies to test applicability on real-world spatio-temporal data.
evidence_signal: The evaluation uses a synthetic ground-truth field with known mean and covariance, enabling direct recovery assessment rather than observation-only comparison.
watch_item: Results may not transfer directly to real data where the true process is unknown, so covariance metrics and controls must be used carefully when interpreting model fidelity.
paper_title: Can Deep Generative Models Reproduce Non-Stationary Gaussian Random Fields?
